newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures rally as sterling falls.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures rally as sterling falls.

text.p: UK wheat futures bounced back towards the close on Tuesday as sterling fell on the foreign exchange markets, traders said.
Wheat futures recovered from as much as one-stg down to close 0.60 stg up.
"It's been all currency today there is no other reason for such a swing in the prices," said a trader.
However, higher futures brought trading in the cash market almost to a standstill.
"We were having a good day until the futures rallied, now it has all stopped," said one physical trader.
Wheat futures closed 0.35 to 0.60 stg up after trading 455 lots. November 1997 which did not trade during the afternoon finished 0.75 stg down.
Barley futures rallied from 1.05 stg down but failed to move into the black and closed 0.10 to 0.30 stg down after trading 57 lots.
In Amsterdam milling wheat futures were neglected.
On the UK physical market Jan feed wheat traded at 96 stg, Jan/Mar at 96.50 and Apr/Jun at 98 stg a tonne in coasters fob east coast ports prior to the rally on the futures market.
Delivered market traders reported active trading during the morning, but here too business was brought to a halt by the higher futures.
Feed wheat in East Anglia was fetching 95.50 stg for Jan and 98.50 stg for Apr/Jun.
On the west coast Jan traded at 95 stg and Jan/Mar at 96 stg.
Feed barley was trading at 95 stg for Jan in East Anglia and 96.0 stg in the Avon area for Jan/Mar.
Milling wheat 11-percent protein fetched 118 stg for Jan/Mar in Liverpool and 114 stg in the London area.
